data: The ultrastability ledger, the provenance ledger, the open work items and every other paper's findings
title: Who is the second loop?
paper_title: Who is the second loop? Measuring how often a person has to step in to keep an AI system ultrastable
paper_frame: Ashby's ultrastable system has two loops. The fast one fixes ordinary trouble. The slow one changes the system itself when the fast one can't. We asked who plays the slow loop here, and counted.
summary: For two weeks the owner kept typing the same kind of message: the changelog is quiet, pull requests are stale, papers never got posted. Each one was a person doing the slow loop's job. This paper turns that into numbers: how often a person stepped in, whether the system's own slow-loop changes ever worked, whether its work items could be misread, and whether its own papers are true in its code.

misperception.belief: An AI system that runs itself only needs good monitoring; when something breaks, a probe catches it and a fix follows.
misperception.short: Monitoring plus fixes is enough to run unattended.
misperception.counter: Monitoring fixes instances. Staying viable for a year also needs a loop that changes the rules, thresholds and work specs when the same trouble keeps coming back, and that loop has to be judged on whether its changes work.

findings.concern: A person acting as the slow loop
findings.claim: Every owner message that redirects the system is a slow-loop action done by hand. We count distinct owner-driven sessions that changed the repository in a week; the target is none.

mechanisms.how: owner_interventions reads the provenance ledger every tick as an essential variable with a ladder

findings.concern: A slow loop that never learns
findings.claim: Before this change the slow loop had judged 91 of its own steps and reverted all 91. A loop that only moves is not adapting. Its keep rate is now an essential variable, and its first step on that variable is to change its own settle window.

mechanisms.how: keep_rate reads the loop's own verdicts; the ladder edits settle_ticks and patience_ticks in doctrine/ultrastability.json

findings.claim: A vague item gets a plausible wrong fix. An item passes intake only with a machine-checkable done check, the metric it should move, an out-of-scope line and a live proof step.

mechanisms.how: fails any new open item missing one of the four parts; a shrink-only baseline holds the old ones

findings.concern: Papers the code does not live up to
findings.claim: Each finding in each paper names its mechanism and the measurement that tests it. The share that meets its target is an essential variable, so a paper that drifts from the code pushes the slow loop to build, not to edit the paper.

mechanisms.how: research_findings_met_share measures every finding of every paper
research_in_code holds the share at 1.0 with a build ladder

findings.claim: Every essential variable, including the four added here, has limits, so the slow loop can fire on each.

mechanisms.how: the check fails a variable with no limits
